[LSER.8.8.2] This is required, not cosmetic: where-clause
aggregations re-evaluate on every test with no memoisation
([LEXP.9.2.2]). A read that lazily
evicted or compacted state would be
non-idempotent — the same `p95(t)` read twice at one instant could
differ, and the result would depend on how many rules reference it
(adding an unrelated reader would perturb everyone's value). The
runtime states the implementation rule for every backend at
[RDSC.5a.1a]; the signal backings carry it at [LSIG.2.5].
